problem_solving_method: We chose a simple, straightforward approach using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Python to ensure rapid development and ease of deployment. This stack allowed us to quickly implement all four requirements including OCR receipt scanning, monthly dashboard analytics, AI-powered forecasting and insights, and savings pocket management with DPS calculations. The simplicity of the tech stack made it easier to build, test, and debug within the event timeframe.

R1.evidence: /add-expense-ocr - OCR receipt upload with amount, date, and shop name extraction with user verification

R2.evidence: /dashboard - Monthly dashboard showing total spent vs salary, category breakdown, largest expenses, and month-over-month comparison

R3.evidence: /dashboard - AI-powered forecast showing expected spending, money left/short at month end, and three specific category-based insights

R4.evidence: /savings - Savings pockets with name, target amount, monthly contribution, expected completion date based on forecast, and DPS return calculations

team_members.major_contribution: Complete implementation of Problem 12 - Personal Ledger Manager including all four requirements, frontend and backend development, OCR integration, dashboard analytics, AI forecasting, and savings management
Problem 12 development - collaboration on code development, testing, and integration

major_design_decisions: Used React with TypeScript for type-safe frontend development
Implemented shadcn/ui component library for consistent, accessible UI components
Used SQLite database for lightweight, file-based data persistence
Integrated Tesseract.js for client-side OCR processing of receipts
Implemented OpenAI GPT-4 for generating personalized financial insights and forecasts
Used Recharts library for interactive data visualizations on the dashboard
Created a simple Express.js backend for API endpoints and database operations
known_limitations: OCR accuracy depends on receipt image quality and clarity
Forecast calculations are based on current month data and may not account for seasonal variations
DPS calculations use a fixed interest rate assumption
